chunks: And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone with one another, they say, 'Do you tell them what Allah has revealed to you, so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?' Do you not use reason?

key_terms.عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ: In the presence of your Lord
key_terms.لِيُحَاجُّوكُمْ: So that they may argue/dispute with you

ai.seo_question: How did the hypocrites behave differently in public versus private according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological duality of the Munafiqun, who fear the social and political consequences of open disbelief while harboring internal skepticism. The rhetorical question 'Do you not use your intellect?' (afala ta'qilun) underscores the failure of their reasoning in exposing themselves to divine accountability through their own words. This behavior is often linked to the concept of 'taqiyya' (dissimulation), though here it is portrayed as a flaw rather than a virtue, as it stems from weakness rather than strategic wisdom.
